title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: The US struck Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, hours after a tanker was hit by two projectiles in the Gulf, while Iran floated a 48-hour plan to reopen the strait through Qatari mediators. Shipping is still near a standstill and today's US midterms keep the risk of wider strikes high, so plan for no quick reopening.

stories.headline: US strikes Iranian targets in Hormuz; tanker hit by two projectiles in the Gulf
body: A US official said on Monday the US carried out 'defensive strikes' on some Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, aimed at Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets. Iranian state TV reported explosions on Qeshm Island. The strikes appeared limited; the last known US attacks were in early September.

Hours earlier, at 3:47am UAE time on Monday, UKMTO said a tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles about 72 nautical miles east of Ras Al Khafji, Saudi Arabia. AP says October saw the most attacks on commercial ships in Hormuz since March, and officials warn new strikes could push the Houthis to step up Red Sea attacks.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: the US is firing again and attacks have reached the upper Gulf. Keep war-risk and Gulf sea surcharges in place and do not promise Jebel Ali direct calls.

stories.headline: Iran offers a 48-hour Hormuz reopening plan, but traffic is near zero
body: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, through Qatari mediators, proposed a two-day plan: the US acts on day one, and Iran reopens the strait on day two. It was cut from an earlier seven-day plan and depends on the US ending its naval blockade. No US acceptance has been reported.
IMF PortWatch recorded just 2 transits on 25 October against a pre-crisis 85 a day, and 113 ships were holding position in the Strait and Gulf on Monday. Brent fell 2% to $111.20 on the talk.
stories.soWhat: A deal is possible but not close. Price Q4 contracts for a closed strait and add a clause to cut surcharges if it reopens.

stories.headline: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd's FM1 reaches Khor Fakkan on 16 November
body: The relaunched Gemini FM1 loop runs Qingdao, Ningbo, Tanjung Pelepas, Khor Fakkan and Singapore. Its first sailing, Maersk Athabasca, left Qingdao on 17 October and is due at Khor Fakkan on 16 November. It does not call Jebel Ali; Maersk will serve the Upper Gulf by land.
stories.soWhat: More direct Asia volume is heading to an already jammed Khor Fakkan in two weeks. Pre-book trucking and storage for mid-November arrivals.

stories.headline: Saudi flights: Etihad off until 5 November, Emirates targets 8 November, Indian carriers to 14 November
body: Etihad has cancelled Riyadh, Dammam and some Jeddah flights until 5 November. Emirates plans to resume Riyadh and Dammam on 8 November. IndiGo, Air India and Air India Express have suspended Saudi routes until 14 November, while British Airways resumes Riyadh today with one daily flight.
Dubai is the bright spot: departing seat capacity reached 7.2 million in October, up 23% from June.
stories.soWhat: New: Indian carriers stay off Saudi until 14 November, so India–KSA belly space via the Gulf stays tight. Dubai belly capacity is back, which helps UAE outbound express.

stories.headline: UAE and Canada sign trade deal cutting tariffs on 99% of Canadian exports
body: The UAE–Canada CEPA, signed after a record 47-day negotiation, removes or cuts tariffs on more than 99% of current Canadian exports to the UAE once fully in place. It is expected to take effect in 2027. Both sides aim to double two-way trade from CA$3.4 billion to CA$7 billion over a decade.
stories.soWhat: A new lane to build for 2027. Line up Canada–UAE freight and express pricing with our North America partners before the deal takes effect.
stories.imageCredit: Abu Dhabi Media Office via Arab News

competitors.name: UPS
competitors.headline: Q3 international revenue up 7.1%, revenue per piece up 15%; full-year guidance raised
body: UPS international revenue rose 7.1% to $5.0 billion in Q3, with revenue per piece up 15% and a 14.9% operating margin. Supply Chain Solutions revenue rose 18.2% to $2.98 billion, helped by forwarding and healthcare. UPS raised its full-year guidance to about $92.6 billion in revenue.
competitors.soWhat: Global integrators are growing on price, not volume. That gives us room to hold yield on international express rather than chase share with discounts.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Freighter fleet heading to 23 by March 2027; freighter network above 60 destinations
body: Emirates SkyCargo has taken seven new Boeing 777 freighters since March 2026 plus its first converted 777-300ERSF, and will run 23 dedicated freighters by the end of March 2027. Freighter destinations grew from just over 40 in March to over 60 by July. South American exports rose 18% to more than 22,000 tonnes since April.
competitors.soWhat: Dubai's home carrier is adding main-deck lift fast. Use it: negotiate block space for peak and heavy cargo out of DXB and DWC.
competitors.imageCredit: Emirates SkyCargo via Air Cargo News

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: MoU with GMR Airports for express cargo facilities in India by March 2027; Q3 results pending
body: Aramex signed an MoU with GMR Airports for dedicated truck docks, screening and space at GMR express cargo terminals in India, with built-in customs clearance, aiming for March 2027. Our latest reported result is Q2 2026: revenue up 22% to Dh1.83 billion and net profit of Dh47 million.
competitors.soWhat: India–GCC express is a lane we can grow while Indian airlines stay off Saudi routes; check Q3 numbers against surcharge income when they land.

opportunities.title: Reopening clause as a selling point
opportunities.text: Iran's 48-hour plan means a sudden reopening is possible. Offer contracts with surcharges that fall automatically if Hormuz reopens.

opportunities.title: Khor Fakkan arrivals from mid-November
opportunities.text: FM1 lands at Khor Fakkan on 16 November with no Jebel Ali call. Sell trucking, clearance and storage to its consignees now.

opportunities.title: Dubai belly capacity is back
opportunities.text: Dubai departing seats hit 7.2 million in October, up 23% from June. Use it for UAE outbound express while Gulf freighter space stays short.

opportunities.title: India–GCC express
opportunities.text: Indian carriers are off Saudi until 14 November. Offer India–UAE air plus UAE–KSA road.

opportunities.title: Canada–UAE lane for 2027
opportunities.text: The new CEPA cuts tariffs on 99% of Canadian exports. Start building the product and partner rates.

watchouts.title: Strikes resume around Hormuz
watchouts.text: US strikes on Qeshm and projectiles hitting a tanker near Saudi waters raise the risk to upper Gulf shipping.

watchouts.title: Houthi and Red Sea risk
watchouts.text: Officials warn new US strikes could push the Houthis to step up attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping.

watchouts.title: Post-midterm escalation
watchouts.text: The US votes today; a third US carrier group is heading to the region.

watchouts.title: Khor Fakkan queue to grow
watchouts.text: More direct Asia services are adding calls at a port where ships already wait over a week.

watchouts.title: Oil swings both ways
watchouts.text: Brent dropped 2% on reopening talk but is still above $110; fuel costs can jump again on any escalation.

moves.title: Keep Gulf war-risk surcharges in place
moves.text: Do not cut sea surcharges on reopening talk; Monday saw new strikes and a tanker hit.

moves.title: Add a reopening review clause to Q4 quotes
moves.text: Tie Hormuz surcharges to a trigger so customers see they fall if the strait reopens.

moves.title: Pre-sell Khor Fakkan handling for FM1
moves.text: Contact Asia importers on the 16 November FM1 call with trucking, clearance and storage packages.

moves.title: Hold KSA express on road until Emirates flies
moves.text: Keep Riyadh and Dammam on road at least until 8 November; check Etihad after 5 November.

moves.title: Push India–UAE–KSA combined service
moves.text: Package air into Dubai and road to Saudi for Indian shippers while Indian carriers stay off Saudi routes.

moves.title: Protect international express yield
moves.text: UPS grew revenue per piece 15%; review discounts on our top international accounts before renewals.

moves.title: Ask SkyCargo for peak block space
moves.text: Use Emirates' growing freighter fleet to secure DXB and DWC capacity for November and December.
